name: Food fermentation
desc: Using yeasts and bacteria to make beer, wine, bread and cheese, the oldest biotechnology.

name: Vinegar making
desc: Acetic acid fermentation of alcohol by bacteria, an early controlled microbial process.

name: Selective breeding
desc: Systematic breeding for chosen traits, made methodical by Robert Bakewell's livestock work.

name: Microbiology
desc: Leeuwenhoek's observation of bacteria and protists opened the study of microorganisms.

name: Cell theory
desc: Schleiden and Schwann's principle that all living things are built from cells.

name: Enzymes
desc: Payen's isolation of diastase revealed biological catalysts that drive chemistry in cells.

name: Natural selection
desc: Darwin and Wallace's mechanism of evolution, the organizing theory of biology.

name: Mendelian inheritance
desc: Mendel's pea experiments showed traits pass in discrete units with predictable ratios.

name: Anaerobic digestion
desc: Microbial breakdown of organic waste into biogas, first used at scale in Bombay and Exeter.

name: Pasteurization
desc: Pasteur's gentle heating to kill spoilage microbes, born from his study of fermentation.

name: Autoclave
desc: A pressurized steam sterilizer that made aseptic laboratory culture routine.

name: Pure microbial culture
desc: Koch's methods for growing a single microbial species in isolation.

name: Agar plate
desc: Solid agar growth medium, suggested by Fanny Hesse, for isolating bacterial colonies.

name: Petri dish
desc: Julius Petri's shallow lidded glass dish, the standard vessel for culturing microbes.

name: Tissue culture
desc: Keeping living tissue alive outside the body, first shown by Wilhelm Roux with chick embryo.

name: Cell-free fermentation
desc: Buchner showed yeast extract without living cells could ferment sugar, founding biochemistry.

name: Chromatography
desc: Tsvet's separation of plant pigments on a column, the basis of countless separation methods.

name: Chromosome theory of inheritance
desc: Sutton and Boveri identified chromosomes as the carriers of Mendel's hereditary units.

name: Cell culture
desc: Ross Harrison grew nerve cells in vitro, starting the growth of animal cells outside organisms.

name: Model organism genetics
desc: Morgan's fruit fly lab showed how a fast-breeding species could reveal general genetic rules.

name: Genetic mapping
desc: Sturtevant used recombination frequencies to draw the first linear map of genes on a chromosome.

name: Activated sludge
desc: Aerated microbial flocs that digest sewage, the core of modern wastewater treatment.

name: Bacteriophage
desc: Viruses that infect bacteria, discovered by Twort and d'Herelle and later central to molecular biology.

name: Acetone-butanol fermentation
desc: Weizmann's Clostridium acetobutylicum fermentation producing acetone, butanol and ethanol, used industrially from 1916 for wartime acetone.

name: Industrial fermentation
desc: Large-scale microbial production of chemicals such as citric acid, solvents and enzymes.

name: Hybrid maize
desc: Crossing inbred lines for hybrid vigor, which transformed maize yields.

name: Radioactive tracer
desc: Hevesy's use of radioisotopes to follow molecules through living systems.

name: Ultracentrifuge
desc: Svedberg's high-speed centrifuge for measuring and separating macromolecules.

name: Induced mutagenesis
desc: Muller showed X-rays cause heritable mutations, giving breeders and geneticists a new tool.

name: Bacterial transformation discovery
desc: Griffith found a heritable 'transforming principle' could pass between pneumococcus strains.

name: Electrophoresis
desc: Tiselius separated proteins by their movement in an electric field.

name: Plant tissue culture
desc: Growing plant cells and tissues on sterile media, enabling micropropagation and regeneration.

name: Immunofluorescence
desc: Coons tagged antibodies with fluorescent dyes to locate specific molecules in cells.

name: Bioreactor
desc: Stirred, aerated deep-tank vessels, developed for mass penicillin production.

name: DNA as genetic material
desc: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty showed the transforming principle was DNA.

name: Paper chromatography
desc: Martin and Synge's partition chromatography on paper, used to separate amino acids.

name: Bacterial conjugation
desc: Lederberg and Tatum found bacteria exchange genes by direct contact.

name: Cell fractionation
desc: Differential centrifugation to separate organelles, revealing the cell's internal machinery.

name: Cryopreservation
desc: Freezing cells with glycerol protectant so they survive, enabling cell banks and sperm storage.

name: Transposable elements
desc: McClintock discovered mobile genes in maize that jump within the genome.

name: Edman degradation
desc: Stepwise chemical removal of amino acids from a protein's end for sequencing.

name: Chemostat
desc: Monod and Szilard's continuous culture vessel for holding microbes at steady growth.

name: HeLa cell line
desc: The first immortal human cell line, taken from Henrietta Lacks without consent.

name: Protein sequencing
desc: Sanger determined insulin's amino acid sequence, proving proteins have defined sequences.

name: Lambda phage
desc: A temperate bacterial virus that became a key genetic model and cloning vector.

name: Plasmid
desc: Lederberg named the small extrachromosomal DNA circles that carry genes between bacteria.

name: Somatic cell nuclear transfer
desc: Briggs and King transplanted nuclei into frog eggs, later extended by Gurdon to body cells.

name: Hershey-Chase experiment
desc: Radiolabeled phages confirmed that DNA, not protein, carries genetic information.

name: Gel electrophoresis
desc: Smithies' starch gel separated proteins by size and charge with high resolution.

name: Eagle's medium
desc: A defined nutrient medium that standardized the growth of mammalian cells.

name: Size-exclusion chromatography
desc: Separating biomolecules by size through porous gel beads.

name: Karyotyping
desc: Tjio and Levan counted the 46 human chromosomes, founding clinical cytogenetics.

name: DNA polymerase
desc: Kornberg isolated the enzyme that copies DNA, later a workhorse of molecular biology.

name: CHO cells
desc: Chinese hamster ovary cells, later the main host for producing therapeutic proteins.

name: Central dogma
desc: Crick's principle that sequence information, once in protein, cannot flow back to protein or nucleic acid.

name: Density-gradient centrifugation
desc: Meselson and Stahl's isotope gradient showed DNA replicates semiconservatively.

name: Radioimmunoassay
desc: Yalow and Berson measured tiny hormone levels with radiolabeled antibodies.

name: Stem cells
desc: Till and McCulloch showed bone marrow contains self-renewing cells that form blood lineages.

name: Genetic code
desc: Nirenberg and Matthaei cracked the first codon, leading to the full triplet code by 1966.

name: Cell-free protein synthesis
desc: Making proteins from cell extracts without living cells, used to decode the genetic code.

name: Lac operon
desc: Jacob and Monod's model of gene regulation, later used to switch on engineered genes.

name: Nucleic acid hybridization
desc: Base-pairing of complementary strands, the principle behind probes, blots and arrays.

name: Biosensor
desc: Clark's enzyme electrode for glucose, the first device coupling biology to an electrical readout.

name: Solid-phase peptide synthesis
desc: Merrifield built peptides on resin beads, automating chemical protein synthesis.

name: Single-cell protein
desc: Microbial biomass grown on hydrocarbons or methanol as food and feed protein.

name: DNA ligase
desc: The enzyme that seals breaks in DNA, used to join fragments in cloning.

name: HPLC
desc: High-pressure liquid chromatography for fast, precise separation of biomolecules.

name: Affinity chromatography
desc: Purifying a protein by its specific binding to an immobilized partner.

name: Flow cytometry
desc: Measuring fluorescence of single cells in a stream; cell sorting pioneered by Fulwyler.

name: In situ hybridization
desc: Locating specific DNA or RNA sequences directly in cells and tissue sections.

name: Immobilized enzymes
desc: Enzymes fixed to solid supports for reuse in continuous industrial processes.

name: Restriction enzymes
desc: Smith isolated enzymes that cut DNA at specific sequences, the scissors of genetic engineering.

name: Reverse transcriptase
desc: Temin and Baltimore found the enzyme that copies RNA into DNA, enabling cDNA cloning.

name: Bacterial transformation
desc: Mandel and Higa's calcium chloride method made bacteria take up foreign DNA.

name: SDS-PAGE
desc: Laemmli's denaturing polyacrylamide gels resolve proteins by molecular weight.

name: Sequence alignment algorithms
desc: Dynamic programming to align biological sequences, a foundation of bioinformatics.

name: ELISA
desc: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for detecting proteins with antibodies and a color change.

name: Protein Data Bank
desc: The shared archive of 3D biomolecular structures, later the training data for AlphaFold.

name: Viral vectors
desc: Berg spliced foreign DNA into SV40, starting the use of viruses to deliver genes.

name: Artificial gene synthesis
desc: Khorana's group chemically assembled the first synthetic gene.

name: Agarose gel electrophoresis
desc: Agarose gels for separating DNA fragments by length, routine in every molecular lab.

name: Cloning vector
desc: Plasmids such as pSC101 engineered to carry and replicate foreign DNA in bacteria.

name: Transgenic animals
desc: Jaenisch introduced foreign DNA into mouse embryos, making the first transgenic mammal.

name: Hybridoma technology
desc: Kohler and Milstein fused B cells with myeloma cells to make monoclonal antibodies.

name: Southern blot
desc: Edwin Southern's transfer of DNA from gels to membranes for probe detection.

name: 2D gel electrophoresis
desc: O'Farrell separated thousands of proteins by charge then size, a precursor of proteomics.

name: Bioremediation
desc: Using microbes to break down pollutants such as oil spills and solvents.

name: Patch clamp
desc: Neher and Sakmann recorded currents through single ion channels in cell membranes.

name: cDNA cloning
desc: DNA copies of messenger RNA, letting researchers clone expressed genes without introns.

name: Expression vector
desc: Vectors that make host cells produce a cloned protein, first used for human somatostatin.

name: pBR322
desc: A compact, widely shared plasmid that became the standard E. coli cloning vector.

name: Northern blot
desc: Blotting RNA onto membranes to measure gene expression.

name: Maxam-Gilbert sequencing
desc: Chemical cleavage method of reading DNA, published alongside Sanger's.

name: Site-directed mutagenesis
desc: Michael Smith's method for making precise changes at chosen positions in DNA.

name: Genomic library
desc: Collections of cloned fragments covering an organism's genome, used to find genes.

name: Algae fuel
desc: Growing microalgae for oils and fuels, pursued in the US Aquatic Species Program.

name: Western blot
desc: Transferring proteins to membranes and detecting them with antibodies.

name: RFLP analysis
desc: Using DNA variation in restriction fragments as genetic markers for mapping.

name: Fluorescence in situ hybridization
desc: Fluorescent probes that light up specific DNA sequences on chromosomes.

name: Embryonic stem cells
desc: Evans, Kaufman and Martin derived pluripotent mouse stem cell lines, human lines following in 1998.

name: Oligonucleotide synthesis
desc: Caruthers' phosphoramidite chemistry made automated synthesis of short DNA strands routine.

name: Capillary electrophoresis
desc: Electrophoresis in thin capillaries, later the basis of high-throughput DNA sequencers.

name: GenBank
desc: The public database of nucleotide sequences, a pillar of open genomics.

name: Shotgun sequencing
desc: Sequencing random fragments and assembling them by computer, used for whole genomes.

name: Electroporation
desc: Electric pulses open cell membranes so DNA can enter, a general transfection method.

name: DNA nanotechnology
desc: Seeman's idea of building structures from programmed DNA base pairing.

name: Genetically modified plant
desc: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation produced the first transgenic tobacco plants.

name: Ancient DNA
desc: DNA recovered from the extinct quagga opened genetic study of the past.

name: DNA profiling
desc: Jeffreys' genetic fingerprinting identified individuals from repetitive DNA.

name: Pulsed-field gel electrophoresis
desc: Alternating fields separate very large DNA molecules, even whole chromosomes.

name: Cryo-electron microscopy
desc: Imaging flash-frozen molecules by electron microscopy; atomic resolution arrived around 2013.

name: Phage display
desc: George Smith displayed proteins on phage surfaces to select binders from huge libraries.

name: MALDI mass spectrometry
desc: A gentle laser ionization that lets mass spectrometers weigh large proteins.

name: Protein NMR
desc: Wuthrich solved protein structures in solution by nuclear magnetic resonance.

name: Automated DNA sequencer
desc: Fluorescent dye sequencing machines from Hood's lab and Applied Biosystems.

name: Yeast artificial chromosome
desc: Vectors carrying hundreds of kilobases of DNA in yeast, used for genome mapping.

name: Gene targeting
desc: Capecchi and Smithies used homologous recombination to alter chosen genes in stem cells.

name: CRISPR arrays
desc: Repeats found in bacterial DNA, later understood as an adaptive immune system against phages.

name: Gene gun
desc: Shooting DNA-coated metal particles into cells, used to transform crops such as maize.

name: Lipofection
desc: Felgner's cationic lipids deliver DNA into cells, a precursor of lipid nanoparticles.

name: Taq polymerase
desc: A heat-stable polymerase from hot-spring bacteria that let PCR be automated.

name: Cre-Lox recombination
desc: A phage recombinase used to delete or switch genes in specific tissues or at set times.

name: Electrospray ionization
desc: Fenn's spray ionization brought large biomolecules into mass spectrometry.

name: Tissue engineering
desc: Growing functional tissue from cells on scaffolds, framed by Langer and Vacanti.

name: Knockout mouse
desc: Mice with a chosen gene disabled, the main tool for testing gene function in mammals.

name: Yeast two-hybrid
desc: Fields and Song's yeast assay detects protein-protein interactions.

name: BLAST
desc: Fast heuristic search for similar sequences across databases.

name: Recombinant chymosin
desc: Microbially made rennet for cheese, the first recombinant food enzyme approved.

name: Microfluidics
desc: Manipulating tiny fluid volumes in chips, enabling lab-on-a-chip and droplet assays.

name: Marker-assisted selection
desc: Breeding guided by DNA markers linked to desired traits.

name: Bacterial artificial chromosome
desc: Stable large-insert vectors in E. coli, the backbone of genome projects.

name: Bisulfite sequencing
desc: Chemical conversion that reveals DNA methylation patterns, a key epigenetics method.

name: Tet-On/Tet-Off system
desc: Bujard and Gossen's drug-switchable control of transgene expression.

name: Real-time PCR
desc: Measuring DNA amplification as it happens, for quantifying genes and pathogens.

name: Directed evolution
desc: Frances Arnold's iterative mutation and selection to engineer better enzymes.

name: Green fluorescent protein
desc: Chalfie expressed jellyfish GFP in other organisms, making gene activity visible in living cells.

name: DNA computing
desc: Adleman solved a path problem with DNA molecules, showing biochemistry can compute.

name: CASP
desc: A biennial blind contest for predicting protein structures from sequence.

name: Flavr Savr tomato
desc: A delayed-softening tomato, the first genetically engineered whole food sold.

name: DNA microarray
desc: Chips with thousands of DNA probes to measure expression of many genes at once.

name: Proteomics
desc: Large-scale identification of the proteins in a cell by mass spectrometry.

name: Zinc-finger nuclease
desc: Chandrasegaran fused zinc-finger DNA binders to a nuclease to cut chosen sites.

name: Pyrosequencing
desc: Sequencing by detecting light released as each nucleotide is added.

name: Dolly the sheep
desc: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell, by Wilmut and Campbell at the Roslin Institute.

name: Morpholino antisense
desc: Synthetic antisense oligos that block translation, used to knock down genes in embryos.

name: RNA interference
desc: Fire and Mello found double-stranded RNA silences matching genes.

name: Digital PCR
desc: Splitting a sample into many partitions to count individual DNA molecules.

name: Loop-mediated isothermal amplification
desc: DNA amplification at one temperature, used for simple field diagnostics.

name: Golden rice
desc: Rice engineered to make beta-carotene, an early nutrition-focused GM crop.

name: Synthetic gene circuits
desc: The toggle switch and repressilator showed genes could be wired like electronic circuits.

name: Expanded genetic code
desc: Schultz engineered cells to incorporate unnatural amino acids into proteins.

name: Small interfering RNA
desc: Tuschl showed short synthetic RNAs trigger RNAi in mammalian cells.

name: Chromosome conformation capture
desc: Methods (3C, later Hi-C) that map how chromosomes fold in the nucleus.

name: Human Genome Project
desc: The international effort that produced a reference human genome sequence.

name: BioBricks
desc: Standardized interchangeable DNA parts for assembling genetic systems.

name: Computational protein design
desc: Baker's lab designed Top7, a protein fold not found in nature.

name: 3D bioprinting
desc: Printing living cells and gels layer by layer to build tissue-like structures.

name: Metagenomics
desc: Sequencing DNA from whole environmental samples to study unculturable microbes.

name: iGEM
desc: A student competition in synthetic biology that popularized standard biological parts.

name: Next-generation sequencing
desc: 454 Life Sciences sequenced millions of fragments in parallel, collapsing costs.

name: Optogenetics
desc: Deisseroth and Boyden used light-gated channels to control neurons with precision.

name: Genome-wide association study
desc: Scanning many genomes for variants linked to traits and diseases.

name: Illumina sequencing
desc: Solexa's sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators, the dominant short-read platform.

name: Induced pluripotent stem cells
desc: Yamanaka reprogrammed adult cells into stem cells with four transcription factors.

name: DNA origami
desc: Rothemund folded a long DNA strand into arbitrary shapes with short staples.

name: Brainbow
desc: Random combinations of fluorescent proteins label individual neurons in distinct colors.

name: ChIP-seq
desc: Sequencing DNA bound by specific proteins to map regulatory sites genome-wide.

name: Chemogenetics
desc: Engineered receptors (DREADDs) that let designer drugs switch neurons on or off.

name: RNA-Seq
desc: Sequencing cDNA to measure the whole transcriptome.

name: Golden Gate cloning
desc: One-pot assembly of many DNA parts using type IIS restriction enzymes.

name: Gibson assembly
desc: Isothermal joining of overlapping DNA fragments, used to build synthetic genomes.

name: Exome sequencing
desc: Sequencing just the protein-coding regions to find disease mutations cheaply.

name: Single-cell sequencing
desc: Profiling the genome or transcriptome of individual cells.

name: Organoids
desc: Clevers' lab grew self-organizing mini-intestines from single stem cells.

name: Synthetic genome
desc: The J. Craig Venter Institute booted a bacterium on a chemically synthesized genome.

name: TALEN
desc: Programmable nucleases built from plant-pathogen TALE DNA-binding repeats.

name: SMRT sequencing
desc: Pacific Biosciences' single-molecule long-read sequencing in zero-mode waveguides.

name: Organ-on-a-chip
desc: Ingber's lung-on-a-chip modeled organ function in microfluidic devices.

name: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing
desc: Doudna and Charpentier reprogrammed Cas9 with guide RNA to cut chosen DNA sites.

name: DNA data storage
desc: Church encoded a book in synthetic DNA, a dense and durable storage medium.

name: CLARITY
desc: Making brain tissue transparent so whole organs can be imaged intact.

name: Cultured meat
desc: Mark Post's lab-grown beef burger demonstrated meat from cultured animal cells.

name: Nanopore sequencing
desc: Reading DNA as it threads through a protein pore, in handheld long-read devices.

name: Unnatural base pair
desc: Romesberg's bacteria replicated DNA with a third synthetic base pair.

name: Cellulosic ethanol
desc: Breaking down plant fiber with enzymes into fermentable sugars for fuel.

name: Gene drive
desc: CRISPR constructs that copy themselves to spread through wild populations.

name: Expansion microscopy
desc: Physically swelling samples in hydrogel to see nanoscale detail with ordinary microscopes.

name: Epigenome editing
desc: Using catalytically dead Cas9 fused to modifiers to change gene activity without cutting DNA.

name: Base editing
desc: David Liu's editors change single DNA letters without double-strand breaks.

name: Spatial transcriptomics
desc: Measuring gene expression while keeping its position in tissue.

name: Prime editing
desc: A search-and-replace editor writing new sequence from an RNA template via reverse transcriptase.

name: Xenobots
desc: Computer-designed living machines assembled from frog cells.

name: AlphaFold
desc: DeepMind's deep learning system predicted protein structures near experimental accuracy.
